research_question: Does having children decrease (if at all) the engagement in extramarital affairs?

ivs.description: Presence of children in the marriage (factor indicating whether there are children: 'yes'/'no'). This is the main treatment/predictor of interest.

dv.description: Frequency of engagement in extramarital sexual intercourse during the past year (numeric count coded in the dataset: 0 = none, 1 = once, 2 = twice, 3 = 3 times, 7 = 4-10 times, 12 = monthly/weekly/daily). The analysis also derives a binary any-affair indicator from this column but the canonical outcome column is used here.

controls.description: Respondent age in years (coded into categories: 17.5 = under 20, 22 = 20-24, etc.). Included to adjust for age-related differences in affair rates.
Number of years married (coded categories). Included to adjust for marriage duration effects on affair behavior.
Respondent gender (factor: 'female'/'male'). Included as a demographic control for differences by gender.
Self-reported religiousness (1=anti through 5=very). Included to control for religiosity's association with extramarital behavior.
Education level (numeric coding of highest completed education). Included as a socioeconomic control.
Occupation code (Hollingshead classification). Included as a socioeconomic/occupation control.
Self-rating of marriage happiness (1=very unhappy to 5=very happy). Included to adjust for marital satisfaction/confounding with affairs.

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
from scipy import stats


def main():
    df = pd.read_csv('affairs.csv')

    # Binary indicator for any affair
    df['any_affair'] = (df['affairs'] > 0).astype(int)

    # Descriptive stats by children
    mean_affairs = df.groupby('children')['affairs'].mean()
    rate_any = df.groupby('children')['any_affair'].mean()

    # Welch t-test on affair counts by children
    no_affairs = df.loc[df['children'] == 'no', 'affairs']
    yes_affairs = df.loc[df['children'] == 'yes', 'affairs']
    ttest = stats.ttest_ind(no_affairs, yes_affairs, equal_var=False)

    # Logistic regression: any affair with controls
    logit = smf.logit(
        'any_affair ~ C(children) + age + yearsmarried + C(gender) + religiousness + education + occupation + rating',
        data=df
    ).fit(disp=0)

    # OLS as a robustness check on count outcome
    ols = smf.ols(
        'affairs ~ C(children) + age + yearsmarried + C(gender) + religiousness + education + occupation + rating',
        data=df
    ).fit()

    print('Mean affairs by children:')
    print(mean_affairs)
    print('\nAny-affair rate by children:')
    print(rate_any)
    print('\nWelch t-test (affairs ~ children):')
    print(ttest)
    print('\nLogit coefficients:')
    print(logit.params)
    print('\nLogit p-values:')
    print(logit.pvalues)
    print('\nOLS coefficients:')
    print(ols.params)
    print('\nOLS p-values:')
    print(ols.pvalues)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
